Class JwtAuthenticationToken

java.lang.Object
org.springframework.security.authentication.AbstractAuthenticationToken
org.springframework.security.boot.jwt.authentication.JwtAuthenticationToken
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Principal, org.springframework.security.core.Authentication, org.springframework.security.core.CredentialsContainer
public class JwtAuthenticationToken extends org.springframework.security.authentication.AbstractAuthenticationToken
Spring Security AbstractAuthenticationToken carrying the authentication-time credentials of a JSON Web Token (JWT) login attempt.

This token is produced by the JWT authentication entry-point and is consumed by an AuthenticationManager (or a dedicated AuthenticationProvider). Its lifecycle mirrors the canonical UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken: an unauthenticated instance is built from the raw request payload, then a second authenticated instance is constructed by the manager once the JWT signature has been validated and the principal has been resolved.

In addition to the standard principal/credentials pair, the token carries a few optional request-side hints:

  • sign — the request parameter signature used by the replay-protection layer;
  • longitude / latitude — the latest known geo-location of the user device, which may be validated by a location-aware authentication provider.

For authorization flows that only require a principal (already trusted), prefer JwtAuthorizationToken.

Since:
3.0.0

[@Loong Wan](https://github.com/loong10k)

  • Constructor Details

    • JwtAuthenticationToken

      public JwtAuthenticationToken(Object principal, Object credentials)
      Builds an unauthenticated token from the raw principal/credentials pair extracted from the incoming request. AbstractAuthenticationToken.isAuthenticated() returns false for instances created through this constructor.
      Parameters:
      principal - the user identity to authenticate; typically a username or user-id string, never null.
      credentials - the credentials proving the principal's identity, usually a JWT bearer string, never null.

    • JwtAuthenticationToken

      public JwtAuthenticationToken(Object principal, Object credentials, Collection<? extends org.springframework.security.core.GrantedAuthority> authorities)
      Builds a trusted (already-authenticated) token. Should only be invoked by an AuthenticationManager or AuthenticationProvider implementation that has just verified the JWT signature.
      Parameters:
      principal - the resolved principal (often a UserDetails), never null.
      credentials - the original bearer token; may be null if the manager has already erased sensitive material.
      authorities - the granted authorities for the authenticated user, may be null or empty when the user has no role mappings.

    • setAuthenticated

      public void setAuthenticated(boolean isAuthenticated) throws IllegalArgumentException
      Always rejects a true transition — callers must construct a fresh authenticated token via JwtAuthenticationToken(Object, Object, Collection) instead.
      Specified by:
      setAuthenticated in interface org.springframework.security.core.Authentication
      Overrides:
      setAuthenticated in class org.springframework.security.authentication.AbstractAuthenticationToken
      Parameters:
      isAuthenticated - true would mark the token as trusted; this implementation refuses and throws.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when isAuthenticated is true.

    • eraseCredentials

      public void eraseCredentials()
      Clears sensitive material from this token. Invoked by the Spring Security framework after the authentication result has been returned to the caller, so that the bearer JWT is not retained any longer than necessary.
      Specified by:
      eraseCredentials in interface org.springframework.security.core.CredentialsContainer
      Overrides:
      eraseCredentials in class org.springframework.security.authentication.AbstractAuthenticationToken
